subject: Stepwise MAP: pricing guardrails, ramp cadence, and usage definitions
messages:
From: John Sullivan <john.sullivan@acme-corp.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0400
Subject: Commercial plan + draft MAP for pilot and ramp

Olga —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to start a simple mutual action plan and surface the commercial guardrails before we move to legal. Two high-level asks from our side:

1) We need a clean definition of billable units — especially how you measure "inference tokens" vs "embedding units" and whether fine-tuning / KV cache warming counts toward committed usage.
2) Pricing protection during the ramp: we want a floor for unit price increases during the 12-month commitment, plus clarity on true-ups if we exceed forecasted commits.

Attached is a skeleton MAP and an initial list of redlines from procurement (they asked me to send it now so we don't get blocked). Can you confirm a proposed ramp cadence (monthly targets) and whether Redwood will accept tiered price protection or prefers waterfall true-ups?

Attachments: MAP_PhasePlan_v3.xlsx (map), Procurement_Redlines_v1.pdf (redlines)

Thanks,
John Sullivan
Senior Director, AI Platforms
ACME Corporation

From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: John Sullivan <john.sullivan@acme-corp.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:07:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Commercial plan + draft MAP for pilot and ramp

John —

Appreciate the clear asks and the docs. Quick response while we pull legal and pricing for formal redlines:

- Billable units: Redwood charges for generated tokens (per-token) and separate embedding units. We do not charge for KV cache hits when a request is served entirely from the cache; however, cache *warming* requests that execute model inference are billable. We'll add explicit language to the MAP that separates generation, embedding, and cache-warm activity.

- Price protection / true-ups: our standard approach for pilot->commit is a two-stage protection: 
  * Pricing lock for committed units during the fixed term (quarterly cadence)
  * Overage true-up if actual usage exceeds committed tier; true-up executed at the agreed tier rate for the quarter where the overage occurred (not retroactive to prior quarters).

- Ramp cadence: propose a stepwise monthly ramp in the MAP (Pilot month -> 25% commit month 1 -> 50% month 2 -> 100% month 3), with a 30-day review gate after each step. We can make the ramp smoothing configurable per ACME's needs.

I'll attach a short internal note with suggested language for the usage definitions and true-up mechanics. Ben — can you and Aditya weigh in on whether to offer a one-time discount ladder tied to commit milestones (e.g., 5% at 50% commit, 10% at 100%) or instead bake it into an annual volume band? Grace — please pull the SOW template with payment terms.

I'll follow up with a marked-up MAP and a clean redline for legal by COB Thu.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
[attachment: SOW_Draft_v1.pdf (pdf)]

From: Procurement Team <procure@acme-corp.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 23 Jul 2026 11:35:00 -0400
Subject: Fwd: Commercial plan + draft MAP for pilot and ramp — redlines attached

Olga / Ben —

Forwarding procurement's consolidated redlines. Key commercial comments pulled out:

- Definition concerns: Procurement wants the contract to explicitly exclude internal cache repair/replays and monitoring telemetry from billable usage. They also want a clear definition of "user-initiated inference" vs "system-initiated inference" (e.g., background batch jobs) and separate pricing buckets for both.

- Price cap request: ACME asked for a not-to-exceed cap of +8% on unit price increases within the first 12 months of live production, subject to documented CPI adjustments. Redwood's standard lock + overage True-up may not satisfy procurement — they'd prefer a mixed approach: floor guarantee + capped inflation pass-through.

- True-up timing: procurement asks for a 60-day window to reconcile usage before any invoice true-up is applied and for any reconciliation to be subject to dispute rights (30 days).

Attached: ACME_Redlines_v1.docx (docx)

Please review and call with procurement next Tue 10am ET to talk through the gaps.

—Procurement

From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: John Sullivan <john.sullivan@acme-corp.com>, Procurement Team <procure@acme-corp.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, maya.lutz <maya@cloudco.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Jul 2026 09:30:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Commercial plan + draft MAP for pilot and ramp — proposed concessions and next steps

John / Procurement —

Thanks for the detailed redlines. We reviewed with Pricing and Legal overnight; below is a consolidated, negotiable response for the Tue call:

1) Usage definitions (we'll propose contract language):
   - "Billable Inference": any API call that results in model compute on Redwood infrastructure, excluding cache hits that return without model execution.
   - "System-initiated inference": defined as scheduled background jobs initiated by ACME; billable but eligible for a separate discounted batch rate in the MAP.
   - "Monitoring and telemetry": explicitly excluded from billable usage.

2) Price protection and cap:
   - Redwood will guarantee committed-tier pricing for the contracted term (quarterly checkpoints).
   - We can accept a limited not-to-exceed increase of 8% only if changes are driven by external cloud provider cost shocks (with evidence). Otherwise, price increases will be limited to CPI + 3% with 60 days' notice.

3) True-up mechanics and dispute window:
   - True-ups applied per quarter. ACME will have a 60-day reconciliation window after quarter close to raise disputes. Disputes stay the invoice while under review; if unresolved after 30 days, standard collections apply.

4) Commercial concessions (proposal):
   - Performance ramp discounts: milestone credits — 5% credit at 50% of committed monthly run-rate; 10% credit at sustained 100% for two consecutive months. Credits apply to future invoices, not retroactive.
   - One-time implementation credit tied to successful pilot acceptance (acceptance criteria in MAP).

Next steps:
- I'll upload a marked MAP and a brief redline response doc before EOD Mon so you have time to review the Tue call materials.
- Proposed Tue call: 10:00am ET to walk procurement redlines and align on language we can send to each side's legal teams.

If that sounds OK, Ben/Aditya/Grace and I will join Tue 10. Ben — please confirm you'll own the ramp discount math and provide the sample invoice showing how credits & true-ups flow.

Best,
Olga
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0144
